subtopics.title: Two Models — Relative Frequency and Theoretical Probability

questions.question: The theoretical probability model may only be used when:
options: The experiment has been repeated many times
All outcomes of the experiment are equally likely
The probability is bigger than a half
The event involves dice specifically

questions.question: A taxi association logs 500 trips; 60 arrive late. The relative frequency of lateness is:
As the number of trials grows, the relative frequency of an event:
options: Settles toward the true probability
Always increases toward 1
Becomes more jumpy
Equals the theoretical probability exactly after 100 trials

questions.question: For predicting whether it rains tomorrow, the appropriate model is:
options: Theoretical, because rain either happens or it does not — fifty-fifty
Neither — rain has no probability
Theoretical, because weather is symmetric over the year
Relative frequency, because the outcomes are not equally likely and data must be used

subtopics.title: Venn Diagrams and the Addition Rule

questions.question: When filling in a Venn diagram, you should always start with:
options: The largest circle
The region outside both circles
The intersection — the overlap
The circle mentioned first in the question

questions.question: With 70 music streamers, 50 gamers and 30 doing both among 120 learners, the number doing NEITHER is:
The addition rule states P(A or B) equals:
options: P(A) + P(B)
P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B)
P(A) × P(B)
P(A) − P(B) + P(A and B)

questions.question: The subtraction in the addition rule exists because:
options: Probabilities must always be reduced to lowest terms
The sample space must be excluded
The or-event is always smaller than either event
The overlap is counted once in each circle, so adding the circles counts it twice

questions.question: Events A and B are mutually exclusive exactly when:
options: P(A and B) = 0 — they cannot happen together
P(A) = P(B)
A and B are independent

questions.question: For complementary events, which TWO conditions must both hold?
options: Equal probabilities, and both bigger than zero
No overlap, and together they fill the whole sample space
No overlap, and each has probability one half
They fill the sample space, and they are independent

questions.question: On one die roll, 'multiple of 4' and 'odd' are mutually exclusive but NOT complementary because:
options: They overlap at the outcome 4
Their probabilities are equal
The outcomes 2 and 6 belong to neither event, so the two do not fill the sample space
A die cannot show a multiple of 4

questions.question: The complement shortcut says P(at least one late taxi this week) equals:
options: P(exactly one late taxi)
P(no late taxis) − 1
The sum of the probabilities of every possible number of late taxis
1 − P(no late taxis at all)

subtopics.title: Independent Events and the Product Rule

questions.question: Events A and B are independent exactly when:
options: P(A and B) = 0
P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B)
P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B)
A and B share at least one outcome

questions.question: Drawing two cards WITHOUT replacement gives dependent events because:
options: Cards are not symmetric objects
The pack was shuffled before the first draw
The first draw changes the composition of the pack for the second
Two draws always give dependent events, even with replacement

questions.question: In the school data, P(music) × P(gaming) ≈ 0,243 while P(both) = 0,25. The conclusion is:
options: The events are not independent, because the product test demands exact equality
The events are independent, because the numbers are close
The events are mutually exclusive
The test is inconclusive without more learners

questions.question: Two mutually exclusive events with nonzero probabilities can never be independent because:
options: Their circles overlap too much
Exclusive events always have equal probabilities
Independence requires the events to fill the sample space
If one happens, the other's probability crashes to zero — maximal influence, not none

subtopics.title: Guessing from Symmetry or Counting the Tally

questions.question: The friend claiming fifty-fifty for buttered bread misuses the theoretical model because:
options: Bread has more than two sides
The two outcomes are not equally likely — the slice is lopsided
Probability cannot be applied to food
The sample space is infinite

questions.question: From 100 drops with 63 landing butter-down, the relative frequency estimate is:
The tally is described as 'jumpy at first, honest in the long run' because:
options: Relative frequency wobbles over few trials but settles near the truth over many
Early trials are usually recorded wrongly
Probability changes as the experiment continues
Long experiments always give exactly the theoretical value

questions.question: Which situation belongs to the THEORETICAL model's home ground?
options: Whether a soccer team wins its next match
Whether a taxi arrives late tomorrow
Whether it rains on Saturday
Drawing a card from a well-shuffled standard pack

subtopics.title: Two WhatsApp Groups and the Double-Counted Friends

questions.question: Adding the music group's 70 to the gaming group's 50 fails as a headcount because:
options: Some learners belong to no group
The 30 people in both groups are counted twice
Groups cannot be added in probability
The school roll was counted in a different year

questions.question: The honest headcount of learners in at least one group is:
The minus term in the addition rule exists purely to:
options: Cancel the double-counting of the overlap
Make the probability smaller than 1
Remove the people outside both circles
Convert counts into percentages

questions.question: The addition rule may drop its minus term only when:
options: The two events are independent
The sample space is larger than 100
One event lies completely inside the other
The events share no outcomes at all — mutually exclusive

questions.question: After five heads in a row, the probability of heads on the sixth flip is:
options: Less than a half — tails is now due
More than a half — the coin is on a streak
Exactly a half — the coin has no memory
Impossible to say

questions.question: The feeling that tails is 'owed' after a run of heads is called:
options: The addition rule
The gambler's fallacy
Complementary reasoning
The law of large numbers

questions.question: For independent events, P(heads then heads) = ½ × ½ because:
options: Multiplication always gives smaller answers
The events are mutually exclusive
The two flips share the same sample space
Half the futures have heads first, and of those, half have heads again

questions.question: The product-rule 'lie detector' declares two data events dependent when:
options: The product of their probabilities differs from their actual and-probability
The product of their probabilities is less than a half
Their circles overlap on the Venn diagram
Their probabilities are unequal
